records.source: Καὶ ὅταν ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν ἑβδόμην, ἐγένετο σιγὴ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὡς ἡμιώριον.
records.gloss: And when he opened the seal the seventh, there was silence in the heaven about half an hour.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the seventh seal, heaven fell silent for about half an hour.

L.1: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.

R.1: When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, everything in heaven was silent for about half an hour.

decisions.choice: silence in heaven: awe before God acts
alternatives: a silence so that the prayers of the saints can be heard (8:3-4)
decisions.reason: The praise of chapters 4-7 stops. The prophets call for silence before the Lord as he comes to judge: "Be silent before the Lord GOD, for the day of the LORD is near" (Zephaniah 1:7; compare Habakkuk 2:20; Zechariah 2:13). The silence may also make room for the prayers that rise in 8:3-4.

decisions.choice: when: a single event
decisions.reason: ὅταν usually means "whenever", but here it is used with a past verb for one event, as "when".

decisions.choice: the seventh seal opens into the seven trumpets
decisions.reason: The seventh seal brings no horse or disaster of its own. Out of its silence come the seven angels with trumpets (8:2), so that the trumpets unfold what the last seal holds.

records.heading: The seventh seal and the golden censer

records.source: καὶ εἶδον τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλους οἳ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἑστήκασιν, καὶ ἐδόθησαν αὐτοῖς ἑπτὰ σάλπιγγες.
records.gloss: And I saw the seven angels who before the God stand, and were given to them seven trumpets.
pieces: And I saw the seven angels who stand in God's presence; they were given seven trumpets.

L.2: And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.

R.2: Then I saw the seven angels who stand in front of God. They were given seven trumpets.

decisions.choice: the seven angels who stand before God
decisions.reason: The article, "the seven angels", suggests a known group. Jewish writings of the time speak of seven angels who stand in God's presence: in Tobit 12:15 Raphael calls himself "one of the seven angels who stand ready and enter before the glory of the Lord", and 1 Enoch 20 names seven archangels.

decisions.choice: trumpets: signals of war, alarm and the day of the Lord
decisions.reason: Trumpets called Israel to battle and to festivals, and they sounded at the fall of Jericho (Joshua 6). The prophets announce the day of the Lord with a trumpet blast (Joel 2:1; Zephaniah 1:14-16).

records.source: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἦλθεν καὶ ἐστάθη ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἔχων λιβανωτὸν χρυσοῦν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ θυμιάματα πολλὰ ἵνα δώσει ταῖς προσευχαῖς τῶν ἁγίων πάντων ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ χρυσοῦν τὸ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου.
records.gloss: And another angel came and stood at the altar having a censer golden, and was given to him incenses many so that he will give with the prayers of the saints all on the altar the golden the [one] before the throne.
pieces: Then another angel came, holding a gold censer, and took his place at the altar. Much incense was handed to him, so that he could add it to the prayers of all God's holy people on the gold altar before the throne.

L.3: And another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer, and much incense was given to him, so that he might offer [it] with the prayers of all the saints on the golden altar that [is] before the throne.

R.3: Another angel came and stood at the altar. He had a gold pan for burning incense. He was given a lot of incense to offer to God along with the prayers of all God's people. He offered it on the gold altar in front of the throne.

decisions.choice: a censer and the golden altar: the altar of incense
decisions.reason: λιβανωτὸν was a vessel for carrying burning coals and incense. The golden altar stood before the inner room of the tabernacle and temple, and incense was burned on it morning and evening (Exodus 30:1-10). In heaven it stands before God's throne.

decisions.choice: the incense is added to the prayers
alternatives: the incense is the prayers, as in 5:8
decisions.reason: "Offer with the prayers" most likely means that the incense goes up together with the prayers and carries them to God. In 5:8 the incense is the prayers; the picture is close.

decisions.choice: the prayers of all the saints, including the martyrs' cry of 6:10
decisions.reason: The prayers of God's people (5:8) include the cry of the martyrs under the altar for justice (6:9-10). What follows in 8:5 is God's answer.

decisions.choice: censer (L, B); pan for burning incense (R)
decisions.reason: Readable describes the vessel, since few young readers know the word "censer".

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

records.source: καὶ ἀνέβη ὁ καπνὸς τῶν θυμιαμάτων ταῖς προσευχαῖς τῶν ἁγίων ἐκ χειρὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: And went up the smoke of the incenses with the prayers of the saints out of hand of the angel before the God.
pieces: The smoke of the incense rose with the prayers of God's holy people from the angel's hand before God.

L.4: And the smoke of the incense went up with the prayers of the saints from the hand of the angel before God.

R.4: The smoke from the incense went up to God from the angel's hand, together with the prayers of God's people.

decisions.choice: prayer rising like incense: Psalm 141:2
decisions.reason: "Let my prayer be counted as incense before you" (Psalm 141:2). The prayers of God's people reach him.

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

records.source: καὶ εἴληφεν ὁ ἄγγελος τὸν λιβανωτόν, καὶ ἐγέμισεν αὐτὸν ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ ἐγένοντο βρονταὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ ἀστραπαὶ καὶ σεισμός.
records.gloss: And has taken the angel the censer and filled it out of the fire of the altar and threw to the earth, and there were thunders and voices and lightnings and earthquake.
pieces: The angel then took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and flung it onto the earth. Thunder crashed, there were loud sounds and lightning, and the earth shook.

L.5: And the angel took the censer and filled it with the fire of the altar and threw [it] to the earth, and there were thunders and voices and lightnings and an earthquake.

R.5: Then the angel took the incense pan and filled it with fire from the altar. He threw it down on the earth. There was thunder, loud noise, lightning, and an earthquake.

decisions.choice: fire thrown on the earth: Ezekiel 10
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel 10:2 a man clothed in linen fills his hands with burning coals from between the cherubim and scatters them over Jerusalem in judgment. The same altar from which the prayers rose sends down fire: the prayers of the saints are answered in judgment.

decisions.choice: thunder, voices, lightning and earthquake
decisions.reason: The signs of God's presence at Sinai and around the throne (4:5) now come to the earth, with an earthquake added. The list grows at each stage (11:19; 16:18-21).

decisions.choice: voices (L); loud sounds (B); loud noise (R)
decisions.reason: As in 4:5, the word means loud sounds or rumblings.

records.source: Καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ ἄγγελοι οἱ ἔχοντες τὰς ἑπτὰ σάλπιγγας ἡτοίμασαν αὑτοὺς ἵνα σαλπίσωσιν.
records.gloss: And the seven angels the [ones] having the seven trumpets prepared themselves so that they might blow trumpets.
pieces: Then the seven angels holding the seven trumpets made ready to blow them.

L.6: And the seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to blow [them].

R.6: Then the seven angels who had the seven trumpets got ready to blow them.

decisions.choice: the trumpets now begin
decisions.reason: After the interruption of 8:3-5, John returns to the seven angels of 8:2. The first four trumpets (8:7-12) strike the natural world; the last three are announced as "woes" (8:13).

records.heading: The first four trumpets

records.source: Καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἐγένετο χάλαζα καὶ πῦρ μεμιγμένα ἐν αἵματι, καὶ ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῆς γῆς κατεκάη, καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν δένδρων κατεκάη, καὶ πᾶς χόρτος χλωρὸς κατεκάη.
records.gloss: And the first blew trumpet, and there was hail and fire having been mixed in blood, and it was thrown to the earth; and the third of the earth was burned up, and the third of the trees was burned up, and all grass green was burned up.
pieces: When the first angel blew his trumpet, hail and fire, mixed with blood, were flung down on the earth. A third of the land was burned up, and a third of the trees, and every green blade of grass.

L.7: And the first blew his trumpet, and there was hail and fire mixed with blood, and it was thrown to the earth, and a third of the earth was burned up, and a third of the trees was burned up, and all green grass was burned up.

R.7: The first angel blew his trumpet. Hail and fire mixed with blood were thrown down on the earth. A third of the earth burned up. A third of the trees burned up. All the green grass burned up.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: hail and fire
decisions.reason: The trumpets recall the plagues God sent on Egypt before the exodus (Exodus 9:23-25). As then, God judges a power that oppresses his people, and those he has sealed are spared (7:3; 9:4).

decisions.choice: a third: judgment that is severe but partial
decisions.reason: The seals struck a quarter of the earth (6:8); the trumpets strike a third. The harm is great but not complete. These judgments are warnings that call people to repent, as 9:20-21 shows, before the final judgment.

decisions.choice: all green grass
decisions.reason: Here all the green grass burns, yet in 9:4 the locusts are told not to harm the grass. The visions are pictures of judgment and do not form a single sequence of events in which each detail must agree with the last.

decisions.choice: blew his trumpet
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to blow a trumpet. Every level says so plainly; "his trumpet" is supplied.

records.source: Καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ὡς ὄρος μέγα πυρὶ καιόμενον ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ τρίτον τῆς θαλάσσης αἷμα, καὶ ἀπέθανε τὸ τρίτον τῶν κτισμάτων τῶν ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, τὰ ἔχοντα ψυχάς, καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν πλοίων διεφθάρησαν.
records.gloss: And the second angel blew trumpet, and as a mountain great with fire burning was thrown into the sea; and became the third of the sea blood, \v 9 and died the third of the creatures the [ones] in the sea, those having lives, and the third of the ships were destroyed.
pieces: Then the second angel blew his trumpet. What looked like a great mountain on fire was hurled into the sea, and a third of the sea became blood.
Of the creatures living in the sea a third died, and of the ships a third were wrecked.

L.8: And the second angel blew his trumpet, and [something] like a great mountain burning with fire was thrown into the sea, and a third of the sea became blood,
L.9: and a third of the creatures in the sea, those that had life, died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.

R.8: The second angel blew his trumpet. Something like a huge mountain on fire was thrown into the sea. A third of the sea turned into blood.
R.9: A third of the living things in the sea died. A third of the ships were destroyed.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: water turned to blood
decisions.reason: The trumpets recall the plagues God sent on Egypt before the exodus (Exodus 7:20-21). As then, God judges a power that oppresses his people, and those he has sealed are spared (7:3; 9:4).

decisions.choice: a burning mountain: Jeremiah's word against Babylon
decisions.reason: God calls Babylon a "destroying mountain" and says he will make it "a burnt mountain" (Jeremiah 51:25). The picture may hint at the fall of a great power. John says only that it was "like" a mountain.

decisions.choice: a third: judgment that is severe but partial
decisions.reason: The seals struck a quarter of the earth (6:8); the trumpets strike a third. The harm is great but not complete. These judgments are warnings that call people to repent, as 9:20-21 shows, before the final judgment.

decisions.choice: blew his trumpet
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to blow a trumpet. Every level says so plainly; "his trumpet" is supplied.

records.source: Καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀστὴρ μέγας καιόμενος ὡς λαμπάς, καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν ποταμῶν καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς πηγὰς τῶν ὑδάτων.
records.gloss: And the third angel blew trumpet, and fell out of the heaven a star great burning like a torch, and it fell on the third of the rivers and on the springs of the waters.
pieces: The third angel blew his trumpet, and down from the sky came a huge star, burning like a torch. It landed on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water.

L.10: And the third angel blew his trumpet, and a great star fell from heaven, burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of waters.

R.10: The third angel blew his trumpet. A huge star fell from the sky. It was burning like a torch. It fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water.

decisions.choice: a star falling from heaven
alternatives: an angel, as the star in 9:1 is
decisions.reason: Isaiah 14:12 speaks of the king of Babylon as a star fallen from heaven. In 9:1 a fallen star is a being who is given a key. Here the star is the means of the plague, and its name tells what it does (8:11).

decisions.choice: blew his trumpet
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to blow a trumpet. Every level says so plainly; "his trumpet" is supplied.

records.source: καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ ἀστέρος λέγεται· ὁ Ἄψινθος.
records.gloss: And the name of the star is called the Wormwood.

L.11: And the name of the star is called Wormwood.

R.11: The name of the star is Wormwood. Wormwood is a very bitter plant.

decisions.choice: Wormwood: a bitter plant, a picture of judgment
decisions.reason: Wormwood is a plant with a very bitter taste. In the prophets it stands for the bitterness of God's judgment: "I will feed this people with wormwood and give them poisonous water to drink" (Jeremiah 9:15; 23:15).

decisions.choice: Wormwood is a very bitter plant (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

records.source: καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ τρίτον τῶν ὑδάτων εἰς ἄψινθον, καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπέθανον ἐκ τῶν ὑδάτων, ὅτι ἐπικράνθησαν.
records.gloss: And became the third of the waters into wormwood, and many of the people died from the waters because they were made bitter.
pieces: A third of the waters turned to wormwood, and many {{gender:people|men}} died from the water, because it had been made bitter.

L.11: And a third of the waters became wormwood, and many of the {{gender:people|men}} died from the waters, because they had been made bitter.

R.11: A third of the water became bitter like wormwood. Many {{gender:people|men}} died from drinking the water, because it was bitter.

decisions.choice: bitter water: Marah reversed
decisions.reason: At Marah God made bitter water sweet for Israel (Exodus 15:23-25). Here sweet water is made bitter and deadly. Wormwood itself is not a deadly poison; the picture is of water turned so bitter that it brings death (compare Jeremiah 9:15).

decisions.choice: people: men and women
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων means human beings in general.

decisions.choice: people | men
decisions.reason: The gender setting, since the word includes everyone (m2).

records.source: Καὶ ὁ τέταρτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἐπλήγη τὸ τρίτον τοῦ ἡλίου καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῆς σελήνης καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀστέρων, ἵνα σκοτισθῇ τὸ τρίτον αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ ἡμέρα μὴ φάνῃ τὸ τρίτον αὐτῆς, καὶ ἡ νὺξ ὁμοίως.
records.gloss: And the fourth angel blew trumpet, and was struck the third of the sun and the third of the moon and the third of the stars, so that would be darkened the third of them and the day not would shine the third of it, and the night likewise.
pieces: Then the fourth angel blew his trumpet. A blow fell on a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, and a third of their light was darkened: for a third of the day nothing shone, and so too for the night.

L.12: And the fourth angel blew his trumpet, and a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them would be darkened, and the day would not shine for a third of it, and the night likewise.

R.12: The fourth angel blew his trumpet. Then a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars were struck. They became dark. So there was no light for a third of the day and for a third of the night.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: darkness
decisions.reason: The trumpets recall the plagues God sent on Egypt before the exodus (Exodus 10:21-23). As then, God judges a power that oppresses his people, and those he has sealed are spared (7:3; 9:4).

decisions.choice: a third darkened: dimmer, or dark for a third of the time
decisions.reason: The sentence says both that a third of the lights are darkened and that the day does not shine for a third of its length. The picture is not meant to be worked out like an eclipse; it is a partial darkness, as in Amos 8:9, where God makes the sun go down at noon.

decisions.choice: blew his trumpet
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to blow a trumpet. Every level says so plainly; "his trumpet" is supplied.

records.source: Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἤκουσα ἑνὸς ἀετοῦ πετομένου ἐν μεσουρανήματι λέγοντος φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Οὐαὶ οὐαὶ οὐαὶ τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῶν λοιπῶν φωνῶν τῆς σάλπιγγος τῶν τριῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν μελλόντων σαλπίζειν.
records.gloss: And I saw, and I heard one eagle flying in mid-heaven saying with a voice loud: Woe woe woe to those dwelling on the earth from the remaining voices of the trumpet of the three angels the [ones] being about to blow trumpet.
pieces: Then I looked, and I heard an eagle flying high overhead call out in a loud voice: "Woe, woe, woe to those who live on the earth, at the blasts of the trumpets that the three remaining angels are about to blow!"

L.13: And I looked, and I heard an eagle flying in mid-heaven, saying with a loud voice, "Woe, woe, woe to those who live on the earth, because of the remaining blasts of the trumpet of the three angels who are about to blow!"

R.13: As I watched, I heard an eagle flying high in the sky. It called out in a loud voice, "How terrible! How terrible! How terrible it will be for the people who live on the earth! Three more angels are about to blow their trumpets, and terrible things will happen!"

decisions.choice: an eagle
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "eagle". Some later manuscripts read "angel". The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: an eagle in mid-heaven: a messenger seen and heard by all
decisions.reason: μεσουρανήματι is the highest point of the sky, where the sun stands at noon, so that everyone can see and hear. Hosea 8:1 pictures an eagle over the house of the LORD as a sign of coming judgment. ἑνὸς "one" here means "an".

decisions.choice: three woes for the three trumpets still to come
decisions.reason: "Woe" is a cry of grief and warning. The three woes belong to the fifth, sixth and seventh trumpets (9:12; 11:14). They fall on "those who live on the earth", the world that opposes God (3:10; 6:10).

decisions.choice: Woe (L, B); How terrible (R)
decisions.reason: "Woe" is the familiar word in English Bibles for this cry. Readable says what it means.
